title: LIBERO-Plus: In-depth Robustness Analysis of Vision-Language-Action Models
venue: CVPR 2026 (as 'LIBERO-Plus: A Progressive Robustness Benchmark for Visual-Language-Action Models')
action_head: mixed: discrete action tokens, regression head (OpenVLA-OFT), flow/diffusion action expert (pi0)
methods: single-factor perturbations in 7 dimensions (object layout, camera viewpoint, robot initial state, language, light, background, sensor noise)
blank-instruction and goal-replacement tests of language use
benchmark of 10,030 perturbed tasks with difficulty levels
question: How robust are current VLAs on LIBERO to controlled perturbations, and do they actually use their language and visual inputs as assumed?
key_findings: Camera viewpoint and robot initial state are most damaging: e.g. pi0 94.2% -> 15.8% (camera) and 6.6% (robot init); OpenVLA-OFT 97.1% -> 59.7% and 37.2%; UniVLA 95.2% -> 4.3% under camera change (Table 1).

Language perturbations cause the second-smallest average drop (-25.3 points), but blank-instruction tests show OpenVLA-OFT success on LIBERO-Object is largely unchanged with no instruction, so robustness reflects ignoring language.
Replacing the instruction target with another object in the same scene drops success nearly to zero, and models tend to execute the original task anyway (fixed vision-action mappings).
Models ignore distractors but fail when target objects are displaced, indicating positional rather than semantic object coding.
Wrist cameras confer robustness to viewpoint and illumination changes; co-trained models (pi0, pi0-FAST) are more robust across perturbation types.
Combined perturbations interact (negative compositionality gap), so robustness is not decomposable into single factors.

evidence.scale: per-condition episode counts in appendix (not extracted); 10 model checkpoints
evidence.baselines: unperturbed LIBERO performance of each model

causal_validation: Input-level interventions only (blank instructions, goal replacement, perturbations); no internals.
closed_loop: Yes: closed-loop LIBERO success rates under each perturbation.
limitations_stated: Simulation benchmark; perturbation specifications defined by the authors.
critique: Key behavioral evidence for the review: high LIBERO success can come from vision-action shortcuts that ignore language, which makes 'language-conditioned' interpretability findings on LIBERO-trained checkpoints suspect unless language is shown to matter.
Explains why several batch papers use LIBERO-Plus as a shift benchmark (ProbeAct, SAFECAST, VLA-FAIL).
Blank-instruction finding is reported mainly for OpenVLA-OFT; generality across models is less clear from the main text.
Consistent with 2603.12717's finding that language-dependent goals are concentrated in LIBERO-Goal.
one_line: Systematic perturbations of LIBERO show that strong VLAs collapse under camera or initial-state changes and largely ignore their language instructions, so near-perfect benchmark scores overstate competence.
